result.title: Pythia: Toward Foundation World Models for Multimodal Time Series
result.summary: Time-series foundation models offer a unified approach to forecasting across heterogeneous domains. Textual context and auxiliary observations provide complementary information about temporal dynamics, yet reusable multimodal predictive representations remain underexplored. We introduce Pythia, a foundation world model that learns context-conditioned latent dynamics across datasets through a joint-embedding predictive architecture. A stop-gradient numerical reference guides contextual corrections to predicted future states. A separate probabilistic decoder then adapts to the frozen predictive representation and observed history, decoupling world-model pretraining from observation-space forecasting. On MUSE, Pythia-Tiny's normalized mean absolute scaled error (MASE) and weighted sum quantile loss (WSQL) are 0.6879 and 0.4269, reducing errors by 6.26% and 5.00% relative to the strongest model evaluated in the published MUSE leaderboard. Through a series of controlled experiments, we investigate how to design a time-series world model through shared pretraining and how joint-embedding predictive learning can incorporate multimodal information. The results support separating predictive representation learning from probabilistic readout and show complementary contributions from entity descriptions, events, and covariates.

AI.brief_summary: Pythia 面向多模态时间序列，用联合嵌入预测架构跨数据集预训练上下文条件化的 latent 动力学世界模型，并以 stop-gradient 数值参考引导对未来状态的校正，另用概率解码器适应冻结表示完成观测空间预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 stop-gradient 参考引导的 latent 状态校正、预测表示与读出头解耦，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态更新与答案读出分离、多模态信息注入及表示是否坍缩提供可核查线索；但任务为时间序列预测而非 VLM 推理，需较多迁移判断。
